work_order.confidence_rationale: Six of the seven findings reproduce at lines I read directly in this pass: command-bar.test.ts:9-10 (F7), :68/:69/:88 (F4, F5), :105-106 (F6), :96 (F2's sibling shape), reports.test.ts:241/:266 (F2). F3 does not reproduce — cmdk@1.1.1's published dist has no console output and the lockfile resolves ^1.1.1 to exactly 1.1.1 — so it is dropped rather than implemented. F1 is half true: the missing control-run evidence is real, but 'no automated stage substitutes for it' is a property of .sdlc/config.yml, which is in forbidden_paths. Both review objections against v2 were checked and are conceded in full: the release-note grounds were false and the note is now in files[] matching dbcdcee; AC-6's locator named a comment the pipeline never posts and now names the one it does. What remains uncertain is intent, not code — F4 and F6 each offered two remedies and I picked one, with the alternative argued so a disagreeing reviewer has a defensible option in hand.
work_order.understanding:
Issue #57 collects seven review findings against the command-bar e2e work landed in #48/#53. I re-checked all seven against the tree as it stands now and re-read every line cited below in this pass; nothing has changed on main since v2 of this plan, so the technical work is unchanged. What changes in v3 is the release note (now in scope) and one locator in AC-6.

WHAT REPRODUCES. F2, F4, F5, F6 and F7 are still present exactly as described. packages/desktop-client/e2e/command-bar.test.ts:68 still declares `let settleMatch: () => void;` with no initialiser, assigned only inside the `new Promise` executor at :69-71 and called at :77 inside the `page.on('console')` listener, with `Promise.race([firstDialogWarning, page.waitForTimeout(CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS)])` at :88-91 and `expect(messages).toEqual([])` at :96. F2 is the same defect as the centre of the ticket in a second file: packages/desktop-client/e2e/reports.test.ts:241 attaches a `page.on('pageerror')` listener and :266 reads the buffer, with only `await expect(page).toHaveURL(...)` and two `toBeVisible()` calls between them — every one synchronises on the DOM, none on the CDP channel the errors arrive on. F6 is :105-106 (`toBeTruthy()` plus `not.toBe('Command Bar')`) against the English literals still pinned at :82 and :103. F7 is :9's `(dist/index.mjs:288 and :304)`.

WHAT DOES NOT REPRODUCE. F3 asserts a cmdk console error that does not exist. cmdk@1.1.1's published dist contains no console output, 1.1.1 is what the lockfile resolves (`yarn.lock:11807-11809` pins `cmdk@npm:^1.1.1` to `version: 1.1.1`; packages/desktop-client/package.json:177 declares `^1.1.1`), and grepping the e2e tree for `key prop` and `Each child` returns nothing. The false premise has no footprint in the repository at all: it lives only in the prose of the earlier work order and PR. I record the correction so the next reviewer stops hunting for noise that cannot be generated, and I drop F3 rather than invent a change for it. F1 is half true: the drain really did ship with no execution evidence — `gh pr view 53` shows a body of six unchecked AC boxes and the pipeline footer, with no control output — but 'no automated stage can substitute for it' is a property of this repo's configuration, not a defect fixable inside a ticket: .sdlc/config.yml:172 sets `verify.e2e: ""`, and .sdlc/config.yml is in forbidden_paths. What I can fix is the part that is mine: the drain's central claim was never checked by anything, so I make the test check it on every run.

THE ROOT CAUSE, AND WHY THIS IS ONE TICKET. Every one of these findings is the same bug class: a buffer filled by an out-of-band CDP channel is read after awaits that synchronise on something else entirely. There are exactly two such buffers in the e2e tree — `grep -rn "page.on('console'\|page.on('pageerror'" packages/desktop-client/e2e/` returns only command-bar.test.ts:72 and reports.test.ts:241, and `grep -rn 'toEqual\(\[\]\)' packages/desktop-client/e2e/` returns only those files' two reads at :96 and :266 — so fixing one and not the other would leave the class half-fixed and make the two files disagree about the idiom. No production code changes: CommandBar.tsx:305 renders the Trans producing 'Search pages, accounts and reports' behind the hidden RadixDialog.Description the test guards, and nothing in this ticket touches it.

TWO DECISIONS THE REVIEW LEAVES OPEN. F4 asks for either a justification of the race or its removal; I remove it. The race shortens a failing run by about a second and never changes the verdict — on the passing path both arms of the race wait the full 1000ms, and on the failing path both report `expect(messages).toEqual([])` — and removing it deletes `settleMatch`, `firstDialogWarning` and the non-optional `let` in one go, which dissolves F5 structurally instead of answering it with a comment. F6 asks for either the literal back or all three English literals dropped together; I put the literal back, because the file is pinned to English regardless (lines 82 and 103, and Platform.isPlaywright empties availableLanguages so e2e always renders English), so the literal costs nothing it is not already paying and restores a content check that #39 had and #53 weakened. Dropping all three is a larger, separable change that would ship on its own.

WHAT IS NEW HERE. F1 is the review's sharpest point and it is not satisfied by asking for the same control run a second time — #48 asked, and it did not happen. So instead of a comment alone, the test gains a probe: it emits a message matching its own warning regex at the moment it begins draining, and polls until that message is in a buffer. If the channel stops delivering promptly, the test goes red by itself on every run. That converts a claim nobody was checking into an assertion something checks. Being precise about what that buys: the probe proves the channel delivers into the collector inside the timeout and that the filter still matches the transcribed Radix wording — so an edit to `dialogAccessibilityWarning` that breaks the match, or a CDP delivery regression, both fail loudly. It does NOT prove Radix's current build emits exactly that string, because nothing in the test can make the dialog genuinely unwarned; that remains what the two control runs are for. The probe must be emitted AFTER `expect(messages).toEqual([])` — it matches the same pattern, so run first it would poison the buffer it is meant to be independent of.

WHERE THE EVIDENCE GOES. The control-run output does not go in the PR body. .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md, pulled in by CLAUDE.md as overriding default behaviour, says to create the PR with the unmodified template and never fill it in; and .sdlc/agents/implementer.md:76-79 says the implementer runs with a read-only token, cannot push or comment, and that anything destined for 'the PR body or in a comment' goes in implementer-reply.md at the repo root, which the pipeline posts on the pull request. So both control outputs are written into implementer-reply.md and reach the PR as a posted comment. This is the only channel available to the implementer, and the PR body is not one of them.

THE RELEASE NOTE IS IN SCOPE, and v2's grounds for excluding it were wrong in both directions I checked. `grep -rn 'release-notes-check.mjs' --include=*.yml .` returns exactly one hit, .github/actions/release-notes/check/action.yml:17, and `grep -rn 'release-notes/check' .github/` returns nothing — the composite action is referenced by no workflow, so no gate enforces a note today; sdlc-release.yml's only release-notes step is publish-release-notes.mjs at :141. That much of the old reasoning survives, but the history claim does not: `git log -4 --name-only` shows dbcdcee (#53) added upcoming-release-notes/fix-command-bar-dialog-title-warning.md and 07406d2 (#49) added two more; only 8dffc57 and 51ac962 added none. dbcdcee is the direct predecessor on this exact file, and it shipped a note. Since the check hard-fails any PR that adds no note (release-notes-check.mjs: `if (added.length === 0) reportError(...)`) and rejects bot and agent author lists (findNonPersonAuthors, with NON_PERSON_AUTHORS = ['claude','github-actions'] and a `[bot]` suffix test), the cheap correct move is to match dbcdcee: a one-line Bugfix note crediting a human.
work_order.root_cause: Buffers filled by `page.on('console')` / `page.on('pageerror')` are delivered over CDP out of band, so every await between attaching the listener and reading the buffer must be one that waits on the DOM. Neither test does that: command-bar.test.ts works around it with an over-built race whose payload (`let settleMatch`, `Promise.race`) cannot be proven to be assigned before use and buys nothing, and reports.test.ts:241-266 does not work around it at all. Neither test proves its own drain can do its job, and #53 relaxed the description assertion without removing the English literals that made the relaxed form pointless.
work_order.approach:
Three files, one idiom, no production code.

In command-bar.test.ts:
1. Doc comment: drop `(dist/index.mjs:288 and :304)`, keep the `@radix-ui/react-dialog@1.1.15` pin and both verbatim messages, and say why the version but not the line numbers (F7).
2. Add a module-level `DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE` holding Radix's verbatim description-warning string.
3. Extract the listener into `watchDialogWarnings(page: Page): { messages: string[] }` next to `referredText`, so the test body and the probe share one filter and one type.
4. In the test body: delete `let settleMatch`, `firstDialogWarning` and the `Promise.race([...])`; call `await page.waitForTimeout(CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS)` directly. That is the whole synchronisation point, and it removes F5 with the code rather than around it (F4, F5).
5. Keep `expect(messages).toEqual([])` immediately after the drain — unchanged, and still first so the accessibility assertions below cannot mask it.
6. After that assertion, add the probe: attach a second `watchDialogWarnings`, `page.evaluate` a `console.warn` of `DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE` from inside the page, then `await expect.poll(() => [...probe.messages], { timeout: CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS }).toEqual([DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE])`. Poll, not a second fixed wait, so the cost on a healthy run is one round-trip and not another second (F1). Comment it as what it is: the channel-delivery and filter-match check, not a check that Radix still emits that exact string.
7. Restore `expect(await referredText(dialog, 'aria-describedby')).toBe('Search pages, accounts and reports')`, replacing `toBeTruthy()` and `not.toBe('Command Bar')` — the literal subsumes both, and the string is what CommandBar.tsx:305 renders through i18next's natural-language keys at lng: 'en' (F6).

In reports.test.ts: add a `PAGE_ERROR_SETTLE_MS` constant and a comment naming the same CDP reason, then `await page.waitForTimeout(PAGE_ERROR_SETTLE_MS)` immediately before `expect(pageErrors).toEqual([])` (F2). Same idiom as the sibling file, kept local to each file as the existing `CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS` already is, rather than hoisted into a shared helper for two callers with different channel names.

Then create upcoming-release-notes/fix-command-bar-dialog-console-drain.md, matching the shape and one-line rule of dbcdcee's fix-command-bar-dialog-title-warning.md: front matter `category: Bugfix` (which categoryAutocorrections maps to the valid `Bugfixes`) and `authors: [Shivam-Fl]` — a person, because findNonPersonAuthors rejects `claude`, `github-actions` and any `[bot]` handle — followed by a single line of body with no embedded newline. Do not edit the README and do not edit the existing note.

Finally, run both controls once and write both outputs — the failing run's output showing `expect(messages).toEqual([])` receiving the injected message, and the passing run's output with the drain line deleted — into implementer-reply.md at the repo root, along with a `git status` line confirming the tree is clean afterwards. Do not touch the PR body: .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md forbids filling in the PR template, and the implementer runs with a read-only token that cannot edit it in any case (.sdlc/agents/implementer.md:76-79). The pipeline posts implementer-reply.md on the pull request — .github/workflows/sdlc-implement.yml:616-619 runs `{ echo "## The implementer's answer"; echo; sed 's/^/> /' _out/implementer-reply.md; } | post-comment.mjs pr ...`, so the posted comment's body always begins `## The implementer's answer` and the reply appears beneath it, quoted — which is why AC-6 keys on that header and not on a 🤖 prefix. The probe makes the channel half of control A self-checking from now on, but the second control — that removing the drain makes the test pass — is a property of the drain's presence and is not something a test can assert about itself, so it still has to be run and written down. If the sandbox cannot start the dev server and the controls genuinely cannot be run, say exactly that in implementer-reply.md and name what was attempted; do not report an outcome that was not observed.

risks: The release note credits Shivam-Fl, a human, because findNonPersonAuthors hard-rejects `claude`, `github-actions` and any `[bot]` handle — the agent that writes the file cannot be its own author and the check has no other option. That matches dbcdcee, which credited the same account for the previous change to this same file. If the human who will merge disagrees about attribution, that is a one-line edit to the front matter and it is called out here so it is a decision rather than a surprise in the changelog.

The probe polls for up to CONSOLE_SETTLE_MS. On a heavily loaded machine CDP delivery could occasionally exceed that, producing a flake that fails loudly and correctly rather than passing vacuously — but it is a new flake surface. `expect.poll` defaults to 100ms intervals and returns as soon as the message lands, so the healthy-path cost is one round-trip, not a second.

The probe emits DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE, a transcription of Radix's message held in this file. If a future @radix-ui/react-dialog patch rewords the message, the probe still passes — it exercises the filter and the channel, not Radix. The test would then keep passing while the real warning no longer matches, which is the same blind spot the file had before; the two control runs in AC-6 are what catch it today. Stating this plainly because the alternative reading of the probe is easy to over-claim.
Every run of the command-bar test now spends ~1s of unconditional wall clock that #39 did not. This is the price of the drain the review accepted; the race only ever hid it on green runs.

Restoring the description literal couples the test to an English string in production code. That coupling is pre-existing (lines 82 and 103, and Platform.isPlaywright empties availableLanguages), and i18n.ts uses natural-language keys with fallbackLng: false, so the English render is deterministic under e2e. If the production copy is reworded, this test fails — which is the intended signal, not a false positive.

The control runs may not be executable in the implementer's sandbox if the dev server cannot start. AC-6's how_to_verify says explicitly what to do in that case: record it under coverage_gaps rather than claim an outcome that was not observed. This is the same failure mode #48 had, so it is a live possibility rather than a theoretical one.

No forbidden_path is touched: both test files are under packages/desktop-client/e2e/, and the new note is under upcoming-release-notes/. .sdlc/config.yml is deliberately left alone, so verify.e2e stays empty and no automated stage will ever run these tests. The implementer also does not write the PR body (forbidden by .github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md) and does not commit implementer-reply.md.
No host outside env.api_allowlist is contacted; the changes are local test code and one markdown file.
out_of_scope: Making the e2e suite run in CI (verify.e2e is empty at .sdlc/config.yml:172). This is the real reason F1 had no evidence, and it is unfixable inside a ticket — .sdlc/config.yml is in forbidden_paths. It needs a maintainer decision and belongs in its own issue.

Wiring the unreferenced `release-notes/check` composite action into a workflow so the note becomes an enforced gate. That is the change that would make this note matter mechanically, and it lives under .github/**, which is forbidden to every ticket. The note is added because the repo's own check defines what one looks like and its predecessor shipped one — not because a gate will run it.

work_order.debate_summary:
The review's seven findings are not equally real, and the ticket's own instruction — check each one before planning it, drop what does not hold up — is what separates them. F2, F4, F5, F6 and F7 reproduce exactly as written and are small, precise edits. F3 does not reproduce at all: cmdk@1.1.1's published dist contains no console output and no e2e file references such an error, so the premise has no repository footprint to correct and I drop it rather than manufacture a change. F1 is half real: the missing execution evidence is genuine, but 'no automated stage can substitute for it' is a property of this repo's config, and .sdlc/config.yml is forbidden to this ticket — so the remedy has to be something the test does itself. Hence the probe, which turns the drain's unverified claim into an assertion that fails when the channel stops delivering or the filter stops matching, rather than a control run nobody repeats. Its limit is stated rather than glossed: it cannot prove Radix still emits that exact wording, and AC-6's controls remain the one-time check for that.

The two open decisions were where the review offered a choice. F4 could be answered by justifying the race or by removing it; removal also deletes the non-optional `let settleMatch`, so it resolves F5 structurally instead of by comment. F6 could be answered by restoring the description literal or by dropping all three English literals; restoring is cheaper, loses nothing, and the English render is deterministic in e2e anyway, while the locale-independent version would ship on its own. Both picks are argued above and both alternatives are recorded in alternatives_considered so a disagreeing reviewer does not have to reconstruct them.

The plan review rejected v2 on two points, both conceded in full and both corrected here.

The release-note exclusion was false in both of its stated grounds, and I checked each independently rather than taking either on trust. The invocation site was wrong: `release-notes-check.mjs` is called from `.github/actions/release-notes/check/action.yml:17` and from nowhere else, and `grep -rn 'release-notes/check' .github/` returns nothing, so the composite action is referenced by no workflow and sdlc-release.yml only publishes. The commit history was also wrong: dbcdcee added `fix-command-bar-dialog-title-warning.md` and 07406d2 added two more; the claim that the four most recent commits added none was false. Since one of those two grounds does survive — no gate enforces a note today — the review offered two remedies, and I take the one that costs a markdown file: ship the note, matching dbcdcee's shape, with `category: Bugfix` and a human author because findNonPersonAuthors rejects `claude`, `github-actions` and any `[bot]` handle. That also retires the false claim everywhere it appeared — understanding, out_of_scope and evidence now state the unreferenced-action fact and the real history together, and the prior `NO RELEASE NOTE` sentence is gone.

AC-6's locator was wrong in a way that would have failed a correct change. It told QA to find a 🤖-prefixed comment, but `.github/workflows/sdlc-implement.yml:616-619` pipes a fixed `## The implementer's answer` header followed by the reply quoted with `> `, so a 🤖 prefix on implementer-reply.md lands on the first quoted line rather than the start of the comment. AC-6 now keys on the header the pipeline always emits, names all three things it must carry, and keeps the coverage_gaps fallback. This was the same class of mistake as v1's PR-body channel — a destination chosen by what seemed reasonable rather than by what the pipeline actually does — and it is the reason both channels above are now cited to a line number.

One constraint shaped every acceptance criterion: nothing in CI typechecks or runs these files (packages/desktop-client/tsconfig.json excludes e2e, verify.e2e is empty, vitest's include skips the directory). Criteria about the test files' own logic are therefore verify: test with the exact command named, and only the app behaviour both tests guard is verify: browser. Writing a browser-observable criterion for a test refactor would have been theatre. AC-8 is the one addition: the release note is verified by reading it and running the check script the way the gate would, which is also the honest statement that no gate runs it today.

PR #60's title is `fix: Follow-ups from #48: 7 from the review`, which does not carry the `[AI]` prefix `.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md` requires on every pull-request title. Because GitHub's squash merge reuses the PR title as the commit subject, the merged commit on main will also lack the prefix, unlike `8dffc57`, `07406d2` and `51ac962`.

review.title: The probe re-proves one of `dialogAccessibilityWarning`'s two alternatives, and the one it skips is the one that has actually broken in this file's history. `DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE` holds only the description warning, so `expect.poll(...).toEqual([DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE])` exercises the `Missing .Description. or .aria-describedby` arm and never the `DialogContent. requires a .DialogTitle` arm. The probe's own comments — the constant's doc comment ("the filter still matches the transcribed wording") and the inline block ("an edit that breaks the match turns this test red on every run") — both read as claims about the whole pattern, so a future narrowing of the title arm would leave the probe green while its documentation says otherwise. dbcdcee's second commit in this file was exactly that bug: the shipped pattern had a bare space where Radix's backtick sits, so the title arm could not match, and only the description alternative fired. That is the failure the probe exists to catch, and it is the arm the probe is blind to.
review.detail:
The probe re-proves one of `dialogAccessibilityWarning`'s two alternatives, and the one it skips is the one that has actually broken in this file's history. `DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE` holds only the description warning, so `expect.poll(...).toEqual([DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE])` exercises the `Missing .Description. or .aria-describedby` arm and never the `DialogContent. requires a .DialogTitle` arm. The probe's own comments — the constant's doc comment ("the filter still matches the transcribed wording") and the inline block ("an edit that breaks the match turns this test red on every run") — both read as claims about the whole pattern, so a future narrowing of the title arm would leave the probe green while its documentation says otherwise. dbcdcee's second commit in this file was exactly that bug: the shipped pattern had a bare space where Radix's backtick sits, so the title arm could not match, and only the description alternative fired. That is the failure the probe exists to catch, and it is the arm the probe is blind to.

`packages/desktop-client/e2e/command-bar.test.ts:32`

Evidence: `const DIALOG_WARNING_PROBE = 'Warning: Missing `Description` or `aria-describedby={undefined}` for {DialogContent}.'` at :32-33. The pattern at :21 is `/DialogContent. requires a .DialogTitle|Missing .Description. or .aria-describedby/`. Running both strings against both arms: `alt1.test(probe) === false`, `alt2.test(probe) === true`, `alt1.test(titleMsg) === true`, `alt2.test(titleMsg) === false` — the probe reaches exactly one arm. The title arm's regression history is recorded in dbcdcee's own message: "Radix's title message reads `DialogContent` requires a `DialogTitle` ... — a backtick sits between DialogContent and ' requires', so the pattern shipped with a bare space there could not match it. Only the description alternative fired." The work order's own AC-2 verification mutates only the description alternative ("for example delete the `Missing .Description. or .aria-describedby` alternative"), so neither the check nor the comment distinguishes the two arms.

Fix: Either widen the probe to emit both messages and assert `expect.poll(...).toEqual([TITLE_PROBE, DESC_PROBE])` — or, if a second emitted warning is not wanted, derive the probe constants from the two quoted messages in the doc comment so the regex, the comment, and the probe cannot drift apart. Failing both, narrow the two comments to say "the description arm" rather than "the filter", so the code does not claim coverage it does not have.

qa_open_bugs.title: Dialog-warning probe exercises only one of the two filter alternatives, so it cannot catch a break in the arm dbcdcee actually shipped broken
